_doc: Sickness only comes when something brings it: a plague-bringer's night visit, rats or pilgrims from a plague group's site near town, or a caravan home from a feverish village (any caravan in a plague year). It spreads house to house like fire, slowed by clean water (wells, fountains) and healers (shrine, temple, bathhouse). The sick stay home and are miserable; nobody dies of it.

texts.seed: Sickness at {house}: {why}. A cloth goes up on the door.
texts.cured: A dose of {cure} breaks the fever at {house}.
texts.over: The last of the sick in {town} are up and about. The cloths come down off the doors.
texts.tended: The healers go door to door through the sick lanes, {gold} gold from the treasury. The worst of it should pass in a day or two.
texts.quarantine: The council closes the sick lanes. Nobody in or out but the healers.
texts.lifted: The council opens the sick lanes again.
texts.night: the dead walked there in the night
texts.pilgrims: grey pilgrims from {site} begged at the door
texts.caravan: the caravan home from {settlement} brought a fever with it
